strings.name: Kenneth Rogoff
strings.role: Harvard economics professor and former IMF chief economist
strings.summary: Kenneth Rogoff is an American economist who studies exchange rates, sovereign debt, financial crises and central banking institutions. A former chief economist at the International Monetary Fund, he co-authored This Time Is Different with Carmen Reinhart and continues to write about the dollar’s international role. He also holds the chess grandmaster title.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Current and former chairs and correlation and causation are distinguished; the debt research replication controversy and authors’ response are retained.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies international macroeconomics, debt crises and monetary systems, influencing global policy and academic debate.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a BA and MA from Yale University in 1975 and a doctorate from MIT in February 1980.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current academic chair
strings.facts.f2.value: Harvard economics professor and holder of the Maurits C. Boas Chair of International Economics since January 2022; held the Cabot public policy chair through 2021.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Financial crises across history
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Carmen Reinhart, compared financial crises across countries and historical periods, focusing on debt accumulation and post-crisis adjustment.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Debate over debt and growth research
strings.highlights.h2.text: In 2013, replicators raised calculation, data and weighting issues; the authors acknowledged a calculation error and answered other criticisms. A 90% debt ratio should not be presented as a universal causal law.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Lectured at the Bank of Korea
strings.timeline.t1.text: A Korean-language report confirms a staff lecture on debt supercycles, interest rates and fiscal space; forecasts remain attributed views.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published a book on the dollar
strings.timeline.t2.text: The hardcover and eBook editions of Our Dollar, Your Problem appeared, examining the history and challenges of the dollar’s position; the paperback followed in 2026.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Responded to debt research replication
strings.timeline.t3.text: With Reinhart, acknowledged a calculation error in a figure in their 2010 paper and disputed some methodological criticisms; the controversy involved more than one technical detail.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-authored This Time Is Different
strings.timeline.t4.text: Published a book on the long history of financial crises with Carmen Reinhart.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became IMF chief economist
strings.timeline.t5.text: Also served as director of research, holding the positions until 2003.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Harvard’s faculty
strings.timeline.t6.text: His CV records the start of his economics professorship that month.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earned a doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed his doctorate at MIT with a dissertation on expectations and exchange rate volatility.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Awarded the chess grandmaster title
strings.timeline.t8.text: His 2026 CV retains the title and describes his competitive status as inactive; this is not a current tournament result.
